name: Summer Analyst (intern)
purpose: Learn how a coverage team works by producing supervised inputs to real client work over a fixed internship.
recurring_tasks: Research a client or prospect from public documents
Draft slides or tables from approved content for a senior colleague to edit
Take notes in meetings attended as an observer
Reconcile figures in a pack to their official source
Complete a defined project and present it to the team

can_decide: How to structure their own draft
Which public sources to consult
When to ask for help
can_recommend: Questions the team might ask a client
Improvements to a template or tracker
needs_approval: Any use of client data beyond the task given
belongs_to_others: What is said to a client

measures_of_success: Curiosity shown in the questions asked
Whether the team would want them back
notes: General industry practice for internships in client-facing asset management teams, not a Goldman Sachs statement. The actual content of an internship depends on the team and the supervisor.

name: Analyst
purpose: Own the recurring inputs that let senior colleagues spend their time with clients, and learn the clients and products in depth.
recurring_tasks: Prepare the briefing before each client or prospect meeting
Maintain the pipeline file and the CRM record
Build the first draft of review packs and proposals
Draft RFP and DDQ answers from the approved library
Write up minutes and track actions to completion
Handle routine data requests from clients and consultants
stakeholders: Associates and vice presidents on the team
RFP, reporting and client service teams
Client operations contacts for routine matters

can_decide: Order and method of their own work
When a figure is not safe to send and must be escalated
Routine factual replies using approved material, where the team permits
can_recommend: Which prospects look worth a meeting
What a client is likely to ask
needs_approval: Any commitment on timing made to a client

measures_of_success: Seniors trusting drafts with less rework
notes: General industry practice. At analyst level the day-to-day work on the sales and relationship sides is widely described as similar; that description is plausible but team-specific.

name: Associate
purpose: Run defined pieces of the client process with limited supervision and check the work of analysts.
recurring_tasks: Coordinate an RFP response or a review cycle end to end
Lead preparation for meetings and attend them
Handle day-to-day contact for smaller clients or for the working-level contacts at large ones
Liaise with legal, onboarding and operations on live matters
stakeholders: Vice presidents and the team head

can_decide: How a process is run and sequenced
Routine client replies
Quality sign-off on analyst inputs before senior review
can_recommend: When to escalate a client issue
needs_approval: Messages on performance problems or incidents

measures_of_success: Processes delivered on time without senior rescue
Client contacts choosing to call them directly
notes: General industry practice. The point at which an associate begins to carry their own client list varies widely.

name: Vice President or Executive Director-level coverage professional
purpose: Own a list of clients or a territory and be accountable for its commercial results.
recurring_tasks: Decide which opportunities to pursue and assemble the pitch team
Negotiate fees and terms within approved limits
Manage difficult conversations on performance and service
Forecast flows and report pipeline to management

can_decide: Whether to pursue an opportunity
Meeting strategy and who attends
Routine service matters for their clients

measures_of_success: Retention and growth of the book
notes: Title usage differs by firm and region; do not assume Vice President and Executive Director are separate consecutive levels everywhere. See Chapter 4 for what public sources show.

name: Managing Director, team head
purpose: Set the strategy for a client segment or region, own its largest relationships and be accountable for the team's results and conduct.
recurring_tasks: Sponsor the largest clients and prospects
Approve or escalate pricing and resource requests
Represent the segment's needs to product and investment leadership
Hire, develop and assess the team
stakeholders: Client chief investment officers, trustee chairs and senior consultants

can_decide: Team priorities and coverage allocation
Which searches the team enters
Hiring recommendations within approved headcount

notes: General industry practice. Partner at Goldman Sachs is a separate designation, not simply the next rung for every Managing Director.

name: Institutional sales (business development)
purpose: Win new mandates from institutional asset owners by matching a real client need to a capability the firm can deliver.
stakeholders: Prospects' investment staff, trustees and committees
Relationship managers who will inherit the client

can_decide: Which prospects to prioritise
Whether to compete in a search
How to frame the firm's answer

measures_of_success: Mandates that are still in place several years later
notes: The former intern's label for this side of a team is an unverified account. Titles vary by firm.

name: Institutional relationship management
purpose: Keep existing institutional clients accurately informed and well served so that they can make sound decisions about their mandates.
recurring_tasks: Managing guideline, fee and contract events
stakeholders: Clients' investment staff, trustees, operations and finance teams
Client service, reporting, legal and operations

can_decide: Meeting agendas and who attends
When and how to escalate
Routine service responses
belongs_to_others: The client's decision to stay or leave

measures_of_success: Client feedback and consultant service ratings
notes: Retention is hard to attribute to one person and is not automatically a good client outcome. The former intern's label for this side of a team is an unverified account.

name: Third-party wealth sales
purpose: Get suitable funds researched, approved and adopted by wealth managers, private banks and other intermediaries who invest on behalf of their own clients.
recurring_tasks: Covering fund selectors and research teams
Supplying data in the selector's format
Presenting to advisers and model-portfolio teams

can_decide: Which intermediaries and funds to prioritise
How to support adoption after approval
can_recommend: Which fund suits a selector's search
needs_approval: Fee terms and rebates where permitted
belongs_to_others: The adviser's advice to the end investor

measures_of_success: Number and quality of approved-list positions
notes: An approved-list position is permission to buy, not funded assets. For funds reaching UK retail investors, Consumer Duty obligations apply across the distribution chain.

name: Third-party wealth relationship management
purpose: Keep intermediaries that already hold the firm's funds informed and supported so the funds remain appropriately used.
recurring_tasks: Communicating fund and team changes to all holders
Resolving platform, data and share-class issues
stakeholders: Research teams and committees at intermediaries

can_decide: Order and method of communicating a change, within approved wording
Which holders need a personal call
can_recommend: Alternative funds where an existing one no longer fits
belongs_to_others: The intermediary's decision to hold or remove

measures_of_success: Stability of assets through difficult periods
notes: In many firms one person performs both the sales and relationship functions for a set of intermediaries.

name: Consultant relations
purpose: Make sure investment consultants' research teams understand and can fairly assess the firm's strategies, because their ratings shape which managers asset owners consider.
recurring_tasks: Preparing portfolio managers for research meetings
Briefing sales and relationship colleagues on consultant views
work_products: Internal briefings on searches the firm is or is not likely to see

can_decide: Which strategies to put forward for research and when
How to prepare a team for a research meeting
can_recommend: Whether a search is worth entering given the rating
Changes to how a strategy is explained
needs_approval: Data and materials released to consultants

measures_of_success: Assets won or retained in consultant-advised mandates
notes: UK occupational scheme trustees must set objectives for their investment consultancy providers (in force from 1 October 2022). The consultant is paid by the asset owner and does not invest directly.

name: Product or investment specialist (client portfolio manager)
purpose: Represent an investment team to clients in technical depth, so portfolio managers can spend more time managing money.
recurring_tasks: Feeding client views back to the investment team

can_decide: How to explain the strategy
Content of commentary within approved views
can_recommend: Suitability of the strategy for a client need

measures_of_success: Client and consultant understanding of the strategy
Support for assets raised and retained in the strategy
notes: Sits closer to the investment team than coverage does. Whether specialists hold any investment discretion varies by firm.

name: Client service
purpose: Deliver the operational side of the relationship: reports, data, account maintenance and routine queries.

can_decide: Resolution of routine queries within procedure
Prioritisation of the service queue
can_recommend: When a query is really a commercial issue

notes: The boundary between client service and relationship management differs by firm; some relationship-management seats are close to client service.

name: RFP team
purpose: Produce accurate, compliant written responses to tenders and due-diligence questionnaires.
stakeholders: Content owners across investment, risk, compliance, operations and legal

can_decide: Response process and timetable
Library wording within approved facts
can_recommend: How to answer an ambiguous question
belongs_to_others: The facts themselves, which belong to content owners

measures_of_success: Feedback from sales and from clients' evaluators
notes: A common place for junior coverage staff to contribute: drafting from the library and tracking sign-offs.
